subject: Audit inclusion criteria for runtime modes
messages:
From: Tyler Grant <tyler.grant@finedge.com>
To: irene.choi@redwood.ai
Cc: audit@finedge.com
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: SOC 2 Type II — which runtime modes are in scope?

Hi Irene,

Quick question as we're preparing our vendor attestation packet: does Redwood's SOC 2 Type II (most recent period) cover Dedicated GPU pools and Private/VPC deployments, or is it limited to the Hosted API? Our security team flagged two items:

- Whether the report's control coverage explicitly includes dedicated/reserved customer pools that run under Redwood-managed infrastructure, and
- If Private (customer VPC/on‑prem) deployments can be covered via a bridge letter or any other attestation.

Also—what is the audit period for the Type II you have on file? Our auditor needs exact start/end dates.

Attached is a short list of our questions (SOC2_Requirements.docx) and a sample evidence checklist. If you can point us to the report and any standard bridge language, that would be great. If it's easier, happy to hop on a 20-minute call.

Thanks,

Tyler Grant
Senior Information Security Manager
FinEdge Capital
From: Irene Choi <irene.choi@redwood.ai>
To: Tyler Grant <tyler.grant@finedge.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 15 Nov 2027 10:05:00 -08:00
Subject: Re: SOC 2 Type II — which runtime modes are in scope?

Tyler —

Thanks for the note and for attaching the checklist. Short answer up front:

- Hosted (Redwood API) — fully in scope of our SOC 2 Type II report for the stated period.
- Dedicated (reserved pools) — can be in scope, but only when those pools were explicitly included in the control set for the report period. That depends on whether the dedicated pools were provisioned and onboarded into our monitored environment during the audit window. For some customers with contracts and inventory recorded before the audit cutoff, dedicated pools are included; for pools that came online mid‑period we provide a scoped addendum or bridge letter.
- Private / VPC / On‑prem — generally out of scope for the Redwood Type II because those deployments run in customer‑controlled network environments where we do not operate the underlying host controls. For some managed VPC arrangements where Redwood retains control-plane responsibilities (limited cases), we can evaluate whether a bridge letter or control mapping is appropriate, but it is not the default.

Audit period: 2027-01-01 to 2027-06-30 (SOC 2 Type II). PDF of the report: https://drive.redwood.com/shared/soc2-2027.pdf (I will attach the signed report and a short bridge template).

What we'll need from you to make a firm determination for FinEdge:
1) A list of active deployments during the audit window with deployment IDs and dates (Hosted vs Dedicated vs VPC).
2) For Dedicated pools: the pool IDs and the contract/order date so we can confirm the onboarding timestamp in our inventory.
3) For any Private/VPC you hope to include: a description of cloud/network ownership and which components Redwood manages (control plane, orchestration, patching, etc.).

Next steps — I can draft a customer‑specific bridge letter for dedicated pools that we find were onboarded mid‑period and for managed VPCs where Redwood retained specific operational controls. Marissa will own the evidence exports and Karthik will coordinate the inventory verification.

If you prefer, we can do a short call later today — I have a 30‑minute block at 2:00pm PT.

Best,

Irene Choi
Security & Compliance Manager
Redwood Inference
irene.choi@redwood.ai
+1 415-555-0184
